subject: Astronomy & Space
title: GRS 1915+105: The Speed Demon
description: Learn GRS 1915+105: The Speed Demon in one minute.

hook.text: GRS 1915+105 was the first black hole caught launching jets at apparent superluminal speed—seemingly faster than light.

buildup.text: It's an X-ray binary 28,000 light-years away with a black hole about 12 times the Sun's mass.

discovery.text: In 1994, radio observations showed blobs of plasma appearing to move at 1.25 times the speed of light.

twist.text: It's an illusion. When a jet moves almost at light speed toward you, geometry makes it appear to exceed it.

climax.text: GRS 1915+105 also shows extreme X-ray variability—flickering wildly as it gorges on its companion star's gas.

punchline.text: Faster than light? An optical trick. But the real speed is still terrifying.

quiz.question: Why did GRS 1915+105's jets appear to move faster than light?
options: A geometric illusion occurs when jets move near light speed toward the observer
The black hole's gravity accelerated the jets beyond light speed
Measurement errors in early radio telescopes overstated the speed

details.summary: GRS 1915+105 is a stellar-mass black hole that was the first in our galaxy observed launching jets at apparent superluminal speeds. At about 12 solar masses, it demonstrates the most extreme and erratic X-ray variability of any known black hole, cycling through dramatic accretion states on…
details.whyItMatters: GRS 1915+105 revealed that stellar-mass black holes can launch relativistic jets like their supermassive cousins. Its extreme variability makes it an unparalleled laboratory for studying accretion physics.
takeaways: First galactic black hole observed with superluminal jets
Shows the most extreme X-ray variability known
About 12 solar masses with dramatic accretion state changes

faq.question: Are the jets really moving faster than light?
faq.answer: No — it's apparent superluminal motion, a relativistic illusion. The jets move at about 92% of light speed, but their near-alignment with our line of sight compresses the apparent travel time, making them look faster than light. The effect was first predicted in the 1960s.

faq.question: Why is GRS 1915+105 called a microquasar?
faq.answer: It displays the same phenomena as quasars (accreting supermassive black holes) — accretion disk, relativistic jets, and radio emission — but at stellar scales. Microquasars are scaled-down versions of quasars, evolving on faster timescales that allow real-time study of accretion physics.
